clue.text: Royal figure not quite intent to have post redirected

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: will means intent, as in 'against my will'

indicators.note: post that is redirected is sent on a new route, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: post is mail

explanation.surface: A royal personage who doesn't really mean to have letters forwarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims WILL to WIL; 'redirected' rearranges MAIL into LIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince William is a member of the British royal family, so he is a royal figure.

clue.text: Be an all-rounder — certainly more than a bowler, it seems

definitions.meaning: to fill many roles at once, as an all-rounder does

definitions.text: certainly more than a bowler, it seems
definitions.meaning: a bowler is a hat, so wearing several hats is literally more than one bowler

explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words mislead: an all-rounder both bats and bowls, but here the bowler is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'wear several hats' means to hold many roles, like a versatile player.

clue.text: Kind to put in Greek word for 'printing units'

indicators.note: to put in tells us the kind goes inside the Greek word

parts.note: logos is the Greek for word
a type is a kind or sort

explanation.surface: A sort of thing inserted in a Greek term for printers' pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Logos is the Greek for 'word', familiar from St John's Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Logotypes are pieces of printing type carrying a whole word or several letters cast together.

clue.text: Very interested in historic fiddler, mostly, or singer

parts.note: to be into something is to be very interested in it

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: Someone keen on an ancient fiddler, or perhaps on a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NERO to NER. Nero, the Roman emperor, legendarily played while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoner chants or recites in a sing-song voice, so is a kind of singer.

clue.text: Frozen singer welcoming a warm place to retire?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the singer encloses the letter

parts.note: Mimi in Puccini's La Bohème sings with a frozen hand ('Che gelida manina' is sung to her)

explanation.surface: A singer from Frozen embraces a warm spot for retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frozen' suggests the Disney film; it is Mimi's cold hand in La Bohème. 'welcoming' puts A inside MIMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami in Florida is a famously warm city where many Americans go to spend retirement.

clue.text: Possibly Chesterton's book on Queen bound in gold

indicators.note: bound in means held inside, so the gold surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: gilt is gold, a thin gold covering
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A volume by Chesterton about the monarch, bound in gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' and 'bound' suggest a literary edition, but the definition is Chesterton's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton's given names were Gilbert Keith, so his first name was Gilbert; 'possibly' flags the one name chosen.

clue.text: Follow jet-setter, having dollop of cream, say, on upside-down cake

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the following piece

parts.note: a glob is a dollop, cream being one example

indicators.note: upside-down, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a torte is a rich cake

explanation.surface: A recipe: cream piled on an upside-down cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' turns TORTE into ETROT, placed under GLOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel the world, following the lifestyle of a jet-setter.

clue.text: Hero with weapon avoiding large young feline

parts.note: a lion is a brave person, a hero

indicators.note: avoiding means the weapon goes without the letter for large

parts.note: a club is a weapon

explanation.surface: A hero armed with a weapon, steering clear of a big young cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops L from CLUB, leaving CUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion cub is the young of the lion, a big cat.

clue.text: Water I consumed in rising church centre

indicators.note: consumed in means eaten up within, so the letter sits inside
rising, in a down clue, means the word reads upwards

parts.note: the nave is the central part of a church

explanation.surface: A drink of water taken in the middle of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NAVE to EVAN; 'consumed in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Evian is a well-known brand of French bottled mineral water.

clue.text: Storm's moved inland — you can leave now

definitions.meaning: if the storm has moved inland, the shore is literally free of it
... is said when it is safe to go

explanation.walkthrough: The weather report is the literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the coast is clear' means no one is watching, so it is safe to proceed.

clue.text: Heartless Governments contributing to worker uneasiness

indicators.note: contributing to the worker here means going into the middle of it

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

indicators.note: heartless means the word loses everything but its outer letters

explanation.surface: Governments without compassion add to the anxiety of the working man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributing to' reads as a charade link but signals insertion into the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety, a deep uneasiness.

clue.text: A stance maintained about journal leading one to say sorry

indicators.note: the stance is maintained around the journal, i.e. holds it within

parts.note: poise is a stance or bearing
a log is a journal, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A posture held while writing up a diary that leads someone to apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: The stance is split around the journal; 'leading one to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to express regret, which is what saying sorry does.

clue.text: Observes overturned sack, light

indicators.note: overturned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: notes means observes
to fire is to sack from a job

explanation.surface: Someone notices an upturned bag, quite light in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns NOTES into SETON; 'light' is the verb, not 'not heavy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something, as a fire or bonfire, is to set it on fire: an ignition sense.

clue.text: Cobalt, as it were, is prepared for action

parts.note: cobalt's chemical symbol is Co, two letters side by side, which a phrase could describe letter by letter

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: cobalt is ready to react.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: CAN-DO is 'C and O', which puts together Co, cobalt's symbol; 'as it were' flags this backwards reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-do attitude is eager and ready to get things done, prepared for action.

clue.text: Spray proves air is contaminated

indicators.note: contaminated letters are spoilt and mixed up, so they come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A spray shows the atmosphere is polluted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is contaminated' rearranges PROVES AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaporiser turns liquid into a fine mist, so it is a spray device.

clue.text: Without delay, text offering affection after total damage

indicators.note: after puts the text message below the other pieces

parts.note: a sum is a total
to mar is to damage
ILY is text-message shorthand for I love you

explanation.surface: A loving message sent after a tally of the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: The text-speak abbreviation is a modern touch the solver may not expect in a cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Summarily means promptly and without formalities, at once.

clue.text: Singer needing one in support

indicators.note: in places the one inside the singer

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A singer needs someone to back them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link; 'in' puts I inside BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is a foundation, what something rests on, its support.

clue.text: English to avoid nasty cigarettes, following a plan

indicators.note: nasty cigarettes are spoilt ones, so their letters come out jumbled
to avoid means a letter is kept out of the word

explanation.surface: An Englishman's resolution to steer clear of foul cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' drops one E from CIGARETTES; 'nasty' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategic means planned to achieve a long-term aim, done according to a plan.

clue.text: Make a new start, gaining energy in time off

indicators.note: the time off gains the energy, taking it inside

parts.note: a rest is time off
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone refreshed by a break, coming back with fresh vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' puts E inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to return to a starting state and begin afresh.

clue.text: Openings of three roads use a lot of labour

indicators.note: openings means the first letter of each word

parts.note: avail means use, as in 'of no avail'

explanation.surface: The start of three new roads takes a great deal of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openings of' takes T and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful, exhausting toil, a great deal of hard work.

clue.text: Carpet? Aim for replacement with members' contributions, perhaps

definitions.note: plural: the hand bones that make up part of each arm (a member, or limb)

indicators.note: letters put up for replacement are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: A carpet in need of changing, with fellow members chipping in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' rearranges CARPET AIM. Members' contributions sound like subscriptions; the members are limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Metacarpi are the bones of the hand, so they form part of the arm, a limb or member.

clue.text: Sailor leading pack into church for harvest festival item

indicators.note: into means put inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: leading means coming before the next piece

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a bag is a pack

explanation.surface: A sailor carries a bag into church for the harvest service.
explanation.walkthrough: Harvest festivals, held in British churches each autumn, collect produce such as vegetables for the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabbage is a vegetable, typical of the produce brought to a church harvest festival.

clue.text: Source of wool a lot of shops rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a mall is a lot of shops under one roof

explanation.surface: Many retailers turned down a wool supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns A MALL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is an Andean animal kept for its fleece, a source of wool.

clue.text: Nose? A sort of nose, almost entirely

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a Roman nose is one with a prominent bridge

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a particular type of nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the last letter of A ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In wine tasting the nose is the bouquet or smell, an aroma.

clue.text: Cricketer, one cornered by a reptile, must be agile

indicators.note: cornered by means trapped and surrounded by the reptile

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile
a bat is a batsman in cricket
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricketer trapped by a crocodile would need to be nimble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic means having the nimbleness of an acrobat, gymnastic and supple.

clue.text: Regular behaviour patterns into which son declines

indicators.note: into which means the patterns take the son inside them

parts.note: ruts are fixed, routine ways of behaving

explanation.surface: A son slipping into dull routines and going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into which' puts S inside RUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rust is to deteriorate through neglect, so rusts means declines or decays.

clue.text: Unexpected items in a serving of semolina

indicators.note: a serving of a dish is dished up, so the letters are served in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something odd turns up in a bowl of semolina pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving of' rearranges A SEMOLINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are irregularities or oddities, things that break the expected pattern.

clue.text: View given by theatrical sponsor backing a couple

indicators.note: backing a couple means only the last two letters are turned round

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer of a theatre production

explanation.surface: An opinion from a stage backer who supports a pair of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing a couple' reverses the last two letters of ANGEL, EL becoming LE.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a point of view or perspective on a matter.

clue.text: Journalist-explorer worn-out after going round New York at first

indicators.note: going round means the worn-out word encloses the next piece

parts.note: stale means worn-out, past its best

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An exhausted reporter-adventurer, back from touring New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts N inside STALE; 'at first' takes Y from York, which follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Morton Stanley was a journalist who found Livingstone in Africa and became a famous explorer.

clue.text: Royal name offering small change in second rule

indicators.note: in places the small change between the other two pieces

parts.note: pence are small coins, loose change

explanation.surface: A royal name bringing a minor alteration to a later reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PENCE between S and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Princess of Wales, was born Diana Spencer, so Spencer is a surname tied to the royal family.
